expectations.text: Core goal resolved: spec grants the two CS part-timers access to orders/stats/posts while refunds stay blocked for them, traceable to asked questions
expectations.evidence: FAIL — the core goal is never captured. The interviewer never asked the single requester-answerable, spec-defining question ('who needs access and to which menus'), so per the brief's answer-only protocol the two CS part-timers, their orders/stats/posts need, and the refund block never surface. The spec has no mention of 'CS 알바 2명' or opening orders/stats/posts to them; instead R1.Q4→R2.Q2→R3.Q1 chased the login-infrastructure tangent and the summary concludes the requester shares the owner account so 'enforcement만으로는 실효 0에 가깝다'. The only role model present is an ASSUMED recommended default (owner/manager=주문·환불·공지 / viewer=통계만) that both includes refunds in the manager tier and omits orders/posts from viewer — it does not even encode the actual need, and nothing traces to an asked who/what-access question. Regression vs iterations 3-4 where this question was asked and the core captured.

D1_leverage.evidence: R1 avoids all administrative trivia and every question is architecture-flavored, which keeps it off 0. But leverage ordering fails materially: it led with boss-authority DESIGN axes (role model, refund grantee) that the proxy predictably deferred, and the single highest-leverage, requester-answerable, spec-defining axis — 'who is it for / what access do they need' — was NEVER asked across all three rounds. That omission sank the core goal. Worse than iteration-4 (D1=2) where the same R1 owner-policy lead was recovered by an R2 who-for question; here there is no recovery.

The payment_key/paymentKey territory bug was also flagged (out of scope). Strong UU work.

Every territory claim independently verified accurate against the fixture.

D4_economy.evidence: 8 questions across 3 rounds yet the load-bearing requester-answerable question (who/what access) was never asked; the budget was consumed circling the login/identity axis (R1.Q4→R2.Q2→R3.Q1) — partially defensible adaptive drill-down (R2 detected the shared-account contradiction, R3 resolved it) but a misallocation that spent the entire budget on a tangent and then declared CAPPED. Filler/redundancy present and the core wedge omitted → 1, below iteration-3/4's clean 2.

D5_honest_synthesis.evidence: Given what was elicited, the synthesis is honest and well-partitioned: Decisions/Assumptions/Still Open tripartition with resolution paths, owner-pending flags, and a prominent honest admission that enforcement alone has near-zero effect while the owner account is shared. No fabrication; every claim sourced. The honesty is high even though coverage (core goal) failed — D5 measures the integrity of the synthesis, not completeness.

eval_feedback: Decisive failure: the interviewer never asked the one requester-answerable, core-goal-defining question — 'who needs access and to which menus' — and instead spent all three rounds on the login/identity-infrastructure tangent (R1.Q4 → R2.Q2 → R3.Q1). Because the simulated user answers only what is asked, the two CS part-timers and their orders/stats/posts-not-refunds need never surfaced, so the final spec resolves the wrong thing (concluding the shared owner account makes enforcement pointless) and the core-goal assertion fails. This is a clear regression from iterations 3 and 4, whose winning runs asked the who-for/tasks question (R1 or R2) and captured the core, exactly the ordering risk iteration-4's feedback flagged ('when the requester's authority is unknown, lead with the axes any operator can answer'). Everything the run DID do is strong: proxy/authority handling is textbook (policy axes → pending-owner assumptions, only within-authority items in Decisions), the dormant users.role column and refund irreversibility are territory-anchored and verified, two real unknown-unknowns land, no fabrication, and the CAPPED tag is honestly applied. But the cap is self-inflicted — budget was burned on the identity tangent rather than the core wedge, so CAPPED masks a leverage/economy miss rather than genuinely insufficient budget. 14/15 assertions, rubric 8/10 (D1 and D4 docked for the missed core axis).
